# Carl Meredith

## Overview

- **Age:** Nine years old  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Carl  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034)</sub>

## Appearance

Carl has clear, bright, dark-blue eyes that are direct and fearless, inherited from his late mother. He also shares her brown hair with glints of gold.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)_

## Personality

Carl is a jolly, lovable boy with an intense fascination for natural creatures like bugs, ants, toads, and frogs. He is direct, sturdily courageous, and loyal to his family's honor, willing to face difficult punishments rather than be thought a coward. He is sensitive to his father's feelings and tries to avoid causing him grief.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 c31 P9](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0009), [v5 c31 P10](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0010), [v5 c33 P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027)_

## Traits

- Fearless and direct  <sub>[v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- Fascinated by insects and small animals  <sub>[v5 c2 P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- Lovable and jolly  <sub>[v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- Sturdy and dutiful  <sub>[v5 c31 P10](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0010), [v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knowledge of insects, bees, and small creatures  <sub>[v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>

## History

Thomas Carlyle Meredith, known as Carl, moved to the Glen St. Mary manse with his widowed father, siblings, and Aunt Martha. Passionate about collecting small creatures, he frequently brought bugs, frogs, and ants into the house and kept odd bedfellows like a young garter snake or a lizard in his pocket. While exploring with his family, he often investigated nature, such as ant-beds and dragonflies. After playing in a wet marsh, he suffered a severe sore throat, and on another occasion, he dropped a live eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, which shocked her and upset his father. When a apparent ghost frightened the children in Rainbow Valley, Carl bolted first; to punish himself for cowardice under the rules of their Good-Conduct Club, he spent hours sitting alone on a tombstone in a cold rain until midnight. This ordeal resulted in severe double pneumonia, though he eventually recovered through dedicated nursing and community support. Later, when his father prepared to whip him for the eel incident, the minister saw his late wife's eyes in Carl's face and could not go through with it. Before his father's wedding trip, plans were made for Carl to stay at Elder Clow's.

## Background by volume

- Son of Reverend John Meredith and the late Cecilia Meredith  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- Lost his mother four years prior  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- Slept in a short cot because Jerry refused to share a bed with his animal captives  <sub>[v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
